title: CatBoost evaluates bleeding risk after gastric endoscopic resection
summary: A multicentre retrospective study evaluated post-resection bleeding in 1,084 early-gastric-cancer patients, including 63 bleeding events. CatBoost achieved an internal-test AUC of 0.80, compared with 0.71 for a logistic score. A more detailed early-versus-late bleeding model performed less well. External validation and benefits from model-guided prophylaxis remain untested.

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-data 70:30 internal split with a logistic-score comparator for bleeding within 28 days.
evidence.unknown: External performance, late-bleeding discrimination and preventive clinical benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Categorical boosting learns nonlinear risk from pre/peri-treatment variables and ranks candidate predictors.
